text:
Jordan: CS ticket from Acme Corp — they saw intermittent 502/504s on hosted inference (/v1/generate) starting ~09:12 UTC. High customer impact, multiple failures during billing window. Sending logs now. :eyes:
Priya: Oncall here, ack. Can you paste a failing request and any request IDs? I'll grab traces and start a quick scope.
Jordan: sample curl from customer:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>'
  -d '{"model":"rwd-large-v1","input":"test"}'
```
Request IDs: rq_41f9a2, rq_41f9a3, rq_41f9a4. They reported p95 timeout ~7s then 502.
Priya: Thanks. Quick telemetry: seeing gateway 504s correlated with a spike in seqlen-heavy requests for that tenant at 09:11-09:18 UTC. p90 latency for gateway jumped from 120ms -> 2.3s. Forwarding traces to Luca.
Luca: Runtime check — kernel logs show KV cache miss rate went from 8% -> 68% during the window for the eu-west pool serving that tenant. Also saw batch sizing drop (more small batches) which increases per-token work. Snippet:
```
[kernel] kv_miss_rate=0.68 tenant=acme request_id=rq_41f9a3
[batcher] batch_size=1-3 seq_len=1024-2048
```
Aisha: SRE here — looks like an ingress fanout + large-seqlen client burst. Mitigations we applied at 09:22: (1) temporarily bumped edge keepalive pools for eu-west, (2) enabled fallback routing to smaller quantized model for non-critical paths, (3) added a short per-tenant rate cap so other customers unaffected. Early signals show success — 504s subsided by 09:27.
Jordan: Customer notified at 09:30 with root-cause summary and temporary mitigations, asked for ETA on permanent fix. They appreciated the heads-up but asked for follow-up on SLA exposure.
Kai: Product — do we have count of affected requests / estimated SLA minutes for Acme? Need to prep comms.
Priya: Initial estimate: ~420 failed requests over 6 minutes, approximate affected error budget ~1.2 minutes at p99 SLA (we'll refine). I'm pulling a more accurate query.
Luca: Postmortem notes so far: root cause = tenant burst of long-seq requests causing KV cache churn + smaller batch sizes -> throughput collapse at gateway layer. Secondary factor: no pre-warm for large KV windows on rapid scale-up.
Aisha: Actionable follow-ups proposed:
- A1: Implement per-tenant early backpressure/throttles when KV miss rate > 40% (owner: Priya).
- A2: Add KV warmup prefetch on traffic jumps >x5 sustained for 30s (owner: Luca).
- A3: Batcher heuristic tweak: prefer slightly larger batching for long-seq flows to reduce per-token overhead (owner: Luca).
- A4: CS SDK guidance: recommend client-side max concurrency and sequence-length caps in docs (owner: Jordan).
- A5: Incident playbook update: add a checklist for rapid fallback routing to quantized model + comms template (owner: Aisha).
Jordan: I'll own the customer follow-up and commit to a status update by EOD tomorrow.
Kai: Please add timeline estimates for each action in the postmortem doc. We need an ETA for the KV warmup change and batcher tweak.
Priya: Quick temporary improvement we can make this week: enable a config flag that biases batcher to aggregate sequences up to 200ms window for heavy tenants. Luca — can you scope?
Luca: I can prototype the 200ms aggregator tweak and test on canary within 48h. If it passes perf checks, we can roll to eu-west in next cycle (owner: Luca).
OpsBot: Incident created INC-1759456781, severity=P2, channel=incidents, runbook=hosted-infer-timeouts.
Jordan: Thanks everyone — summary + assigned owners posted in the incident doc. Will schedule a 30-min postmortem meeting tomorrow 11:00 UTC. :+1:
Priya: Closing the immediate war room. Ping if errors reappear.
Aisha: Adding follow-up ticket to SRE backlog for larger infra improvements (ticket SRE-8123).
Jordan: Noted. Thanks team. :heart:
